SERVICE.detail: Two committed records answer this route's service question and they answer it in opposite directions. I can prove the conflict; I cannot resolve it, and a verifier who picked a side here would be doing counsel's job. What the packet says: 'The prosecutor must receive a copy of what you file, by mail or by email', attributed to BCI's Expungement Applicant Instructions, with the packet's form 1146XX, Acceptance of Service – Expungement (Prosecutor), offered for the prosecutor to acknowledge receipt. That attribution is accurate and I verified it from the source bytes — the BCI instructions I rehashed to 9e03980f… head their Step 2 'File the petition with the court and serve the Prosecutor' and carry the line 'Mail or email the prosecutor copies of what you file'. What the committed track registry says, in the entry for track ut_pet_acquittal itself: rules.service reads 'The petitioner does not effect service in the ordinary case: the court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney. The Proof of Service form appears in the published packet only as an optional form, used where the prosecutor's office will not accept service.' It goes further and warns against the very wiring the packet has made: 'The Utah Courts general service-of-process page governs first papers in a new civil case and must not be wired to this track; doing so would import a summons, a process server and a 120-day deadline this track does not have.' rules.notice says the same from the other side: 'The court sends a copy of the filing to the prosecuting attorney.' And the national route-obligation census carries it in the destination detail for both of this route's keys: 'The court sends the filing to the prosecuting attorney; the petitioner does not serve.' So the packet states, as a requirement, a step that two route-keyed committed records say the petitioner does not have. This is not the A3 case — A3 settles what to do when a record is off-point, and here both records are on-point for this exact route — so A3 does not break the tie and I am not going to invent a rule that does.
SERVICE.whyNotScoredAsAFailure: Because I cannot show the packet is wrong. The BCI instructions are the issuing agency's own applicant instructions for Utah expungement, they are held in the corpus, they rehash exactly, and they say what the packet says. It is entirely possible that both are true in practice — the court transmits the filing and BCI advises the petitioner to send copies as well — in which case the packet is merely belt-and-braces and the registry's 'does not serve' is about legal obligation rather than practice. It is also possible the registry is right and the packet imposes a step on a participant that Utah does not require, which is a real cost in effort and a possible source of confusion about the 1146XX form's status. Deciding which needs someone who can read Chapter 40a and URCrP 42 against BCI's page, and that is counsel.
SERVICE.whyNotScoredAsAPass: Because the prior lane failed this obligation citing the registry sentence the packet now contradicts, and passing it silently would bury a conflict the factory has already noticed once. It would also let a family reach a terminal verdict on a participant-facing direction that a committed record denies.
SERVICE.theQuestionForCounsel: On the ut_pet_acquittal route, must the petitioner mail or email the prosecutor a copy of what is filed, as BCI's Expungement Applicant Instructions direct, or does the court transmit the filing to the prosecuting attorney with no service obligation on the petitioner, as the committed track registry and the route census both state? If both are true, which should the packet tell the participant to do, and what is form 1146XX's status — a required acceptance of service, or the optional fallback the registry describes for where a prosecutor's office will not accept service?
SERVICE.whatIsNotInDoubt: The rest of the section is sound whichever way the answer falls. The packet states that the prosecutor or a victim may object and that the participant should attend any hearing the court schedules, which matches the registry's notice rule. It names the Utah State Courts Self-Help Center on 888-583-0009 as a reachable authority. And it handles the certificate correctly: 'Fill in the service method, the address you used and the date only after service has actually happened. A certificate of service dated before service is a false statement, so this packet leaves it blank.' The boundary fixture bears that out — nothing on the service certificate is prefilled.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: Stated, on the standard these four lanes have applied. The packet's first line frames what it is — 'a review fixture built from exact held official Utah forms' — and 'What this packet is not' states the three sentences the passing families in these lanes state: 'It is not legal advice, it is not filed for you, and it does not decide whether the court will grant expungement.' It goes beyond a disclaimer in two places that matter. It names a reachable human authority, the Utah State Courts Self-Help Center on 888-583-0009, in the same breath as the event most likely to need one: 'The prosecutor or a victim in your case may object; if the court schedules a hearing, attend it.' And it draws a boundary around its own knowledge rather than only around its legal status, telling the participant which facts it will not guess and why, and instructing them to ask BCI what the certificates cost rather than assuming. That is the construction on which vt_seal_felony-set and rcap-oh-custom-pleading-clean-tracks were passed in these lanes.
SELF_HELP_STOP.advisory: One held stop condition is missing and it is the strongest one in the registry. The committed track registry lists eight selfHelpStopConditions for this track and marks the first as a hard stop in its own words: 'The participant is not a US citizen. The Utah Courts self-help page itself tells non-citizens to consult an immigration lawyer before expunging, because the FBI may retain records of an expunged case. This is a hard stop, not a caveat.' The packet does not carry it. Of the other seven, the objection-and-hearing condition is addressed in substance and the public-interest-showing condition is partly addressed by requiring the participant to write their own explanation; the remaining five — a BCI special certificate instead of a certificate of eligibility, conviction-counting near the 77-40a-303(4) and (5) limits, an active protective order or stalking injunction, appellate records, and a not-guilty-by-reason-of-insanity verdict — are not carried. I record this rather than failing on it, for the same reason as on my Kentucky and Pennsylvania rows: A1 and A2 confine the establish-then-state ordering to FILING_DESTINATION, FEE_AND_WAIVER and SERVICE, and extending it to SELF_HELP_STOP is a Captain's decision that would move many families at once. But this instance is the sharpest I have seen, because the registry does not merely list the condition — it labels it a hard stop and gives the reason, and the packet is silent on it. If a Captain acts on my cross-family flag anywhere, this is the family to act on first.

CR-410, the order the court signs, ships entirely unchanged — it is one of the three unchanged-official documents and the build writes into it at all. The instructions state the protection as a short explicit list under 'Blanks that are not yours to fill': the order to seal, which the court completes and signs; the attorney block, to be left blank unless a lawyer is filing; and every signature and signature date, which are the participant's at the moment of signing. Naming the attorney block is a good catch — it is a field a self-represented participant would plausibly fill in with their own details.

I walked reports/rendered-artifacts.json and recomputed SHA-256 over every declared file — the sixteen fixture PDFs across four variants and all twenty-four raster page PNGs — and got 40 declared digests, 40 matched, 0 mismatched, 0 missing, with declared byte lengths agreeing. reports/packet-evidence.json independently declares a digest for each document in each packet and those agree too. PAGE_ORDER.detail: This family ships four separate documents per variant rather than one assembled packet, so page order is a question about each document keeping its source's pagination and about the four being presented in a coherent filing order, and both hold. Page counts match the sources throughout: CR-409 at 2 pages, CR-106 at 2, CR-410 at 1, MC-031 at 1, in every one of the four variants, with a committed raster for each page. The presentation order in packet-evidence.json and in the instructions is petition, proposed order, proof of service, attached declaration — which is the order the manifest's own file entry describes, the verified CR-409 filed with the proposed CR-410, with the proof of service following the act it proves.

CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.detail: A clipped run of the official form's own text on the delivered primary filing, present in all four variants, in a family no central visual gate has ever looked at. I found it by measurement and then confirmed it by eye. Running a word-geometry read with pdftotext -bbox over all sixteen delivered fixtures isolates it exactly: the twelve unchanged-official documents have zero words outside the page box, and all four cr-409-filled.pdf fixtures have one, on page 2. The word is 'otection' at x0 -3.442, running off the left edge of the 612-point page. Comparing against the build's own derived source shows what happened. In derived-sources/cr-409-pikepdf-unlocked.pdf the form's viewer notice is set as two lines: 'For your protection and privacy, please press the Clear' at y 756.9 starting at x 36.0, and 'This Form button after you have printed the form.' at y 766.5. In the filled artifact those two lines have been re-flowed into a single line at y 765.1, which is about 74 points too wide for the page, and the overflow has run off the left-hand side — so 'For your pr' is gone and the line begins mid-word. On raster/pc-851-91-matter-of-right-boundary/cr-409/page-02.png it reads 'd privacy, please press the Clear This Form button after you' truncated at the paper's edge and running underneath the green 'Print this form' button. So it is both clipped and overlapping. I am scoring it against the same standard I applied to ny_160_59_petition-set in my other lane, where a word-geometry read plus a raster read established a clipped write and the obligation failed.
CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.severityStatedPlainly: Lower than New York's, and a Captain should weigh it as such. What is clipped here is the form's own viewer chrome — the notice telling a user to press the Clear This Form button after printing — not a participant's name, address or email, and not a substantive line of the filing. Nobody's petition is wrong because of it. What it is, is a delivered page with visibly broken text on it in a Grade-A packet, and a fidelity defect against the official form: the notice is intact and correctly placed in the source and mangled in the artifact. The build damaged text it was not writing into.
CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.whyNothingElseCaughtIt: This family is in RASTER_QUEUE.json's notEligible list rather than its rows, so no central visual gate has ever run on it, and there is no receipt asserting no clipped write. The nine completeness counters read visualDefects 0 because they are not a pixel measurement. The defect sat in every delivered primary filing with nothing positioned to see it.
CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.repair: The fill and flatten path for CR-409 re-flows a two-line static text run on page 2 into one over-wide line and lets it overflow left. Fix the flatten so static content streams are preserved rather than re-laid-out — the original page content streams are byte-identical between the exact source and the pikepdf-unlocked derivative, per this family's own source-fidelity.json, so the damage is introduced after the unlock and is in the writer, not the source. Re-measure with a word-geometry read afterwards, since no central gate will catch a regression here.
CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.fleetRelevance: Worth a Captain's attention beyond this family. The cause is a flatten path applied to an encrypted XFA Judicial Council form, and California's packet families are built from that same class of source. If the writer re-flows static runs generally, other California families built the same way will carry the same defect, and none of them can be checked by the central gate for the same page-parser reason that excluded this one.

FILING_DESTINATION.detail: A recorded failure, properly repaired, and repaired to the record's own words. The defect was that the packet said the court's address was 'not established in this repository' and sent the participant to the clerk, while the committed packet-set manifest held a two-branch venue rule, a filing deadline and a one-arrest-per-petition limit for this exact packetSetId. All three are now stated. The manifest's file entry reads 'File the verified CR-409 with the proposed CR-410 at least 15 days before the hearing, in the court where the accusatory pleading was filed, or where no pleading was filed in a court with criminal jurisdiction in the city or county where the arrest occurred. One arrest per petition.' The packet's 'Where you file this, and by when' section states that sentence. I compared them directly rather than trusting the section heading. Both venue branches are there — the court where the pleading was filed, and the fallback where none was — along with the 15-day deadline and the one-arrest limit. A1's test is answered in the right order: the repository established it, so the packet states it, and it no longer substitutes a question to the clerk for an answer the record holds. The clerk is still named, but now only for what the record genuinely does not hold — the payment methods and any local intake rule.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.detail: Both halves now met, on A3's per-fact test set out in full in feeStandardAmendmentsApplied above. The fee half was already right and remains right: no held record establishes an amount for an 851.91 petition — the compiled profile's on-point line says 'Arrest sealing (851.91) Filing fee varies County Superior Court' and the manifest's pay_fee entry says 'Unresolved and county-specific. Do not publish a figure.' — so the packet publishes none, quotes the manifest's wording, explains that publishing an amount it does not hold would be worse than publishing none, and names the clerk of the Superior Court in the county of the arrest, which is the same office the profile itself names. The waiver half was the recorded defect and is repaired. The earlier finding was that the packet said whether a fee can be waived is 'not established in this repository' while the manifest's apply_fee_waiver entry names FW-001, and that the string FW-001 appeared nowhere in the family directory. It appears twice now, and the treatment is careful in a way that respects A3: it names FW-001 as the general California fee waiver form, says plainly that it is a separate form not included in this packet and not filled in, says where to get it, and then declines to assert what the record does not establish — 'whether a waiver is available on this particular petition, and what it requires of you, is decided on your own financial circumstances and on that court's practice'. Naming a held general form without claiming it necessarily applies to this route is exactly the distinction A3 asks for.

SERVICE.detail: The most consequential of the three recorded failures and the best-repaired. The defect was that the packet said who must be served and by what method were 'not established in this repository' and sent the participant to the clerk — while shipping CR-106, the Judicial Council's own proof of service, with all 33 of its blanks mapped. The earlier finding put it exactly right: the participant had the instrument for proving service, had been told the parties were unknown, and had a 15-day deadline nobody mentioned. All of that is now stated. The manifest's serve_party entry reads 'Serve the prosecuting attorney of the city or county where the arrest occurred, and the arresting agency, at least 15 days before the hearing', and the packet's 'Who you must serve, and by when' section states that sentence. Two named recipients and the deadline. The packet then does two things the finding did not ask for and that make the section work. It explains why CR-106 is in the packet at all — 'it is the proof that you served those parties' — which closes the gap between having the form and knowing its purpose. And it states the ordering rule and the direction the clock runs: 'Serve first, then complete the proof of service — never the other way round. The deadline runs backwards from the hearing, so count from the hearing date, not from the day you file.' A participant who reads that cannot make the two mistakes this route invites.

SELF_HELP_STOP.detail: Stated, and given a section of its own rather than left to a closing line — this family is the only one of my seven with a heading that says 'Where this packet's self-help ends'. The section does three distinct things. It bounds the packet's knowledge: it states what the repository holds for this route and nothing beyond it, and names the filing fee, the payment methods and any local intake rule as things that come from the clerk rather than from the packet. It bounds the packet's role: it does not decide whether the arrest qualifies to be sealed, it does not appear for the participant, and it is not legal advice. And it names two trigger conditions with an instruction attached, which is what separates a stop from a disclaimer: 'If your case does not match the route named at the top of this page, or if anyone opposes the petition, that is the point to get a lawyer or a legal-aid office rather than to press on with these papers.' Opposition is the right trigger to name for 851.91, because an opposed petition is where the interests-of-justice branch turns into an argument. The first line of the packet also states its own status honestly — these are deterministic review fixtures made from exact held official sources and are not approved filing packets — which is the sentence on which an earlier VF02 row passed this obligation for this family, and it is now the least of the reasons to pass it.
